applicable_when: The kernel performs a layout transpose: input has stride (4032000, 1, 32000, 128) — the channel dimension (y0) is stride-1 in memory, but threads iterate over x2 (the spatial dimension) with stride 128 in the load address (y0 + 128*x2 + 4032000*y1). This means consecutive threads in a warp load addresses 128 bytes apart, causing 32x sector amplification and 0% L1 hit rate. Every load misses L1 and hits L2 (96.52% L2 throughput). The fix is to tile the iteration so threads vary over the coalesced (stride-1) dimension on loads, eliminating the sector amplification.
